title: Bias-Aware BiLSTM Toxicity Classifier
summary: The solution tokenizes lowercased comments into word and punctuation tokens, truncates to 220 tokens, and builds a training-only vocabulary of up to 200,000 tokens occurring at least twice. A learned 300-dimensional embedding with spatial dropout feeds two stacked bidirectional LSTMs. Masked mean and max pooling are concatenated, processed by two residual ReLU dense layers, and sent to toxicity and identity-attribute output heads. Training uses weighted binary cross-entropy for toxicity, up-weighting subgroup and subgroup/label-disagreement cases, plus masked multilabel BCE auxiliary identity loss. It uses Adam, mixed-precision gradient scaling, norm clipping, exponential learning-rate decay, and shuffled length-bucketed batches. Validation inference applies sigmoid probabilities in length-bucketed batches; the final output averages validation probabilities from epochs 1 onward. Vocabulary construction and fitting use training rows only, while validation predictions are evaluated by the supplied metric.
